title: Commitment scenario heuristics - 1:1 prep
content:
Context:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with Alex (Head of Dedicated). Goal: land a safe short-term commitment that keeps Q3 throughput flat while buying runway for model onboarding and H100 pilot.

High level ask:
- Propose a 6-month tranche with monthly reconciliation (Q3 start -> Aug 1 onboarding). Ask: 60% baseline commit, 15% headroom credit, 10% burst pool for holidays/launches.
- Rationale: avoids full upfront reserve while giving finance predictable spend and ops predictable capacity.

Concrete numbers (rough heuristics):
- Current baseline: ~240 GPU-hours/day of A100-40 equiv (observed last 30d).
- Target commit (60% baseline): ~144 GPU-hours/day -> ~4 x A100-40 reserved equivalent (rounded).
- Headroom buffer (15%): +36 GPU-hours/day (kept as paid-burst or short-term top-ups).
- Burst pool (10%): ~24 GPU-hours/day for release weeks (metered).
- Translation to H100: 1 H100 ~ 1.7 A100-40 for our inference mix -> if H100 chosen, recommend 3 x H100 + burst.

Autoscale policy options to surface:
- Conservative: strict reserve for baseline, autoscale disabled for reserved pool (burst only on metered). Simpler billing but higher cold-start risk.
- Balanced: reserved baseline + autoscale headroom with capped concurrency (max X instances) and cost alert. Good operational safety.
- Aggressive: low reserve + wide autoscale, rely on preemption fallback to hosted models. Lower cost but higher SLA risk.

Discussion points for 1:1:
- Which SLA tier are we committing to for reserved capacity? (SLO targets and uptime penalties)
- How will rollouts for new models be handled across reserved vs hosted? (pinning strategy)
- Finance: want monthly reconciliation or fixed monthly charge? What does procurement prefer?
- Ops: define a simple playbook for when burst thresholds exceed 3 consecutive days -> trigger review / temporary scale up.

Negotiation anchors (for my ask):
- Anchor 1: 6-month tranche with monthly reconciliation and option to convert unused hours into burst credits for the following month.
- Anchor 2: If customer wants full lock-in, propose a 12-month with 10% discounted rate and committed SLA.
- Walkback: allow conversion between GPU classes within same pool with 72h notice + small swap fee.

Open questions / things to verify before meeting:
- Confirm latest 30d baseline from analytics (ask data team for CSV: mean/95p hourly consumption).
- Verify on-call cost alert thresholds and who owns the pager during burst events.
- Check H100 procurement lead times (hardware team).

Action items to assign (post-call):
- Jordan: squash numbers into a 1-pager and table the three scenarios (conservative/balanced/aggressive) with cost deltas. Due: 48h.
- Riley: pull 30d usage CSV + 95th percentile and run model mix conversion to H100. Due: 24h.
- Sofia: draft a short ops playbook for burst >72h, include runbook links and Slack escalation path. Due: 72h.
- Alex: confirm preferred billing cadence and procurement constraints (follow-up in next meeting).

Notes-to-self (talking bullets):
- Lead with risk framing: "we need predictable inference capacity for three upcoming launches" rather than "we want cheaper capacity".
- Emphasize reversible commitments and conversion flexibility.
- Be ready to show cost impact of committing too little (cold starts, throttling) vs too much (wasted hours).

Quick scenario table (scratch):
- Conservative: reserve 5 x A100-40, no autoscale -> cost +18% vs today, lowest SLA risk.
- Balanced: reserve 3 x H100 (or equiv), autoscale headroom -> cost neutral, moderate risk, best ops fit.
- Aggressive: reserve 2 x H100, wide autoscale -> cost -12%, highest risk.

End of notes. Will convert to tidy 1-pager after the meeting and attach to Confluence.
